court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Family Court at Tiruppur, HMOP No.727 of 2020
facts_of_case: Petitioner and respondent were married in 2012. Two female children were born from the marriage. Due to misunderstanding, they are living separately. Petitioner is unemployed and has to take care of her two female children, making it difficult for her to travel to Tiruppur to contest the case filed by the respondent.

legal_principles.principle: The domicile or citizenship of the opposite party is immaterial in a case like this.
legal_principles.held: In case the marriage was solemnized under Hindu Law marital relationship is governed by the provisions of the Hindu Marriage Act. Therefore, Section 19 has to be given a purposeful interpretation.

legal_principles.principle: The objects and reasons which prompted the parliament to incorporate such a provision have also to be taken note of.
legal_principles.held: Sub Clause (iii-a) was inserted in Section 19 with a specific purpose. Experience is the best teacher.

legal_principles.principle: The place of residence of the wife determines the question of jurisdiction.
legal_principles.held: It is the residence of the wife, which determines the question of jurisdiction, in case the proceeding was initiated at the instance of the wife.

legal_principles.principle: The difficulties faced by women in the matter of initiation of matrimonial proceedings should be considered.
legal_principles.held: Experience is the best teacher. The Government found the difficulties faced by women in the matter of initiation of matrimonial proceedings.

outcome.final_order: The Transfer Civil Miscellaneous Petition was allowed, and the case in HMOP No.727 of 2020 was withdrawn from the file of the Family Court at Tiruppur and transferred to the Additional Sub Court at Kumbakonam.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
use_for_drafting: drafting a transfer petition for divorce case
advising on jurisdictional issues in family courts
